edges.description: At one year the compound mutant improved sensory conduction velocity relative to K562E alone, but did not normalize sensory response amplitude.

edges.description: The model develops severe conduction deficits, myelin thinning, axonal loss, and inflammatory changes. Intrathecal MPZ-promoter AAV9-DNM2 at four weeks increased nerve DNM2 but did not improve the measured outcomes by seven to eight weeks.
edges.limitations: The added Schwann-cell deletion differs from patient heterozygosity. Failure at this dose, timing, promoter, and follow-up does not establish that all DNM2 supplementation is ineffective.

edges.description: Lifelong whole-body Bin1 reduction improved motor performance, muscle organization, and integrin localization in K562E mice. Some improvements persisted to one year, but axonal atrophy and mitochondrial defects were not rescued.
edges.limitations: BIN1 is an experimental modifier here, not an established human modifier. The cross starts before symptom onset and has limited peripheral nerve rescue.
edges.source: Dnm2 K562E mouse with reduced Bin1

edges.description: Muscle-specific DNM2 expression from embryogenesis improved trafficking defects and coordination despite persistent atrophy. Neonatal intraperitoneal AAV9-DNM2 instead worsened muscle pathology and failed to increase nerve DNM2.
edges.limitations: Different expression patterns and developmental timing confound a simple dose-response interpretation. The model has limited neuropathy and provides no evidence of clinical efficacy.
edges.source: Muscle-targeted DNM2 augmentation in Dnm2 K562E mice
